title: Cuando era chavalo
desc: How people talk about the past that was ongoing

sn.s: Don Beto cuenta cómo era antes.
sn.e: Don Beto tells how things used to be.

sn.s: Cuenta de cuando él era chavalo.
sn.e: He talks about when he was a kid.

sn.s: Habla distinto cuando cuenta eso.
sn.e: He talks differently when he tells that.

sn.s: No dice hice ni fui.
sn.e: He does not say I did or I went.

sn.s: Dice hacía y iba y vivía.
sn.e: He says I used to do, I used to go, I used to live.

sn.s: "Yo vivía en el campo", dice él.
sn.e: "I used to live in the countryside," he says.

sn.s: "Nosotros éramos ocho hermanos."
sn.e: "There were eight of us brothers and sisters."

sn.s: "Mi mamá cocinaba para todos."
sn.e: "My mum used to cook for everybody."

sn.s: "Y siempre alcanzaba, no sé cómo."
sn.e: "And there was always enough, I don't know how."

sn.s: Ese pasado es distinto del otro.
sn.e: That past is different from the other one.

sn.s: El otro pasado es para una cosa que pasó.
sn.e: The other past is for a thing that happened.

sn.s: Ayer fui al mercado.
sn.e: Yesterday I went to the market.

sn.s: Este pasado es para cómo eran las cosas.
sn.e: This past is for how things used to be.

sn.s: Antes yo iba al mercado todos los días.
sn.e: I used to go to the market every day.

sn.s: Uno es un momento y el otro es una época.
sn.e: One is a moment and the other is a period.

sn.s: Don Beto sigue contando.
sn.e: Don Beto carries on.

sn.s: "No había luz en el campo."
sn.e: "There was no electricity in the countryside."

sn.s: "Estudiábamos con una lámpara."
sn.e: "We used to study by a lamp."

sn.s: "Yo caminaba una hora a la escuela."
sn.e: "I used to walk an hour to school."

sn.s: "Y una hora de vuelta."
sn.e: "And an hour back."

sn.s: "Y llegaba con hambre siempre."
sn.e: "And I always arrived hungry."

sn.s: Yo escucho sin decir nada.
sn.e: I listen without saying anything.

sn.s: Escucho porque quiero oír los verbos.
sn.e: I listen because I want to hear the verbs.

sn.s: Pero después escucho por la historia.
sn.e: But then I listen for the story.

sn.s: Don Beto dejó la escuela a los once años.
sn.e: Don Beto left school at eleven.

sn.s: Dejó la escuela para trabajar.
sn.e: He left school to work.

sn.s: Trabajaba con su papá en el campo.
sn.e: He used to work with his father in the fields.

sn.s: Trabajaba desde las cinco de la mañana.
sn.e: He used to work from five in the morning.

sn.s: "Éramos pobres", dice él.
sn.e: "We were poor," he says.

sn.s: Lo dice sin pena y sin drama.
sn.e: He says it without shame and without drama.

sn.s: Lo dice como quien dice que llovía.
sn.e: He says it like somebody saying it used to rain.

sn.s: "Ahora es distinto", dice después.
sn.e: "Now it's different," he says afterwards.

sn.s: "Mis hijos fueron a la escuela."
sn.e: "My children went to school."

sn.s: "Uno terminó y trabaja en una oficina."
sn.e: "One finished and works in an office."

sn.s: Eso lo dice con orgullo.
sn.e: That he says with pride.

sn.s: Doña Carmen cuenta lo suyo también.
sn.e: Doña Carmen tells hers too.

sn.s: "Cuando yo era joven todo era más barato."
sn.e: "When I was young everything was cheaper."

sn.s: "Pero tampoco había plata."
sn.e: "But there wasn't any money either."

sn.s: "Uno compraba lo del día y ya."
sn.e: "You bought what you needed for the day and that was it."

sn.s: "Como ahora", dice ella, y se ríe.
sn.e: "Like now," she says, and laughs.

sn.s: Yo trato de contar cómo era mi vida antes.
sn.e: I try to tell them what my life used to be like.

sn.s: Es difícil porque los verbos cambian.
sn.e: It is hard because the verbs change.

sn.s: Digo yo vivía en una ciudad grande.
sn.e: I say I used to live in a big city.

sn.s: Digo yo trabajaba en una oficina.
sn.e: I say I used to work in an office.

sn.s: Digo yo no conocía a mis vecinos.
sn.e: I say I did not know my neighbours.

sn.s: Cuando digo eso, todos me miran.
sn.e: When I say that, everybody looks at me.

sn.s: "¿No conocía a sus vecinos?", dice doña Carmen.
sn.e: "You didn't know your neighbours?" doña Carmen says.

sn.s: "No", digo yo. "A ninguno."
sn.e: "No," I say. "Not one."

sn.s: Ella se queda callada un momento.
sn.e: She stays quiet for a moment.

sn.s: "Qué triste", dice al final.
sn.e: "How sad," she says at the end.

sn.s: Y yo antes no lo veía así.
sn.e: And I never used to see it that way.
